messages:
nina: Intake: onboarding 'cerberus-13b-32k' for prod trial. Need a concise quant plan (int8 / fp8 / gguf hybrid) and a prioritized bring-up checklist. Primary concerns: Spanish hallucination cases, long-context token memory, and 2x cost reduction target. :wave:

nina: TL;DR proposal: smoke eval -> per-layer sensitivity sweep (int8) -> fp8 fallback on highest-sens-attn layers -> gguf conversion + calibration -> end-to-end prompt/regression eval. Need owners and timeline.

dmitri: +1. Can you paste the baseline perf/quality numbers (fp16) and target latency/cost?

nina: baseline fp16 @ 13b: 12.4 tokens/s on p4d, avg latency 170ms/token, spanish-f1 (in our testset) 78.6. Cost target: ~50% token cost vs fp16.

sam: Suggest split into 3 lanes: smoke, sensitivity, and regression. Quick checklist I usually use:
- smoke run (tiny set)
- full calib set sampling (1k prompts)
- per-layer MSE/logit-diff sweep (identify hot layers)
- hybrid plan (fp8 for attn/ffn where needed)
- gguf build + a/b eval
- rollback/fallback route config in serving

sam: Quick smoke commands (local):
```bash
python tools/quant_calib.py --model cerberus-13b-32k --mode int8 --samples 256 --out /tmp/cerb_calib.pkl
python tools/convert_to_gguf.py --model cerberus-13b-32k --quant int8 --calib /tmp/cerb_calib.pkl --out cerberus-int8.gguf
```

eva: For Spanish hallucination, we should add targeted prompt suite (legal/finance/medical) and a factuality metric (QA F1 + hallucination rate). I can assemble 200 targeted prompts by EOD if someone confirms.

nina: please do, @eva. Also we need a light-weight eval harness for long-context (32k): measure prefix-cache warming and KV cache token growth effects.

eval-bot: smoke-int8-2026-03-20: ran 256 prompts -> PPL +10% vs fp16; spanish-f1 -2.7 pts; avg latency -22% (good). Full logs: https://ci.redwood/test/cerb/smoke/2401007890

dmitri: That smoke result looks within the expected band. Next: run per-layer sensitivity sweep. Use these flags to dump per-layer activation diffs and logit-delta heatmap:
```bash
python tools/sensitivity_sweep.py --model cerberus --precision int8 --calib /tmp/cerb_calib.pkl --out /tmp/cerb_sens.json --layers 0-39
```

sam: If certain attention matrices spike > threshold (we use 0.8 logit-delta ROI), plan to keep those layers in fp16/fp8. Hybrid scheme example: keep attn.{6,7,12} in fp16, quant rest -> expect ~40-55% cost drop.

nina: Ops question: if we roll hybrid, can serving auto-fallback to fp16 for rare high-sens requests? @oncall-ops

oncall-ops: Yes — we can route by policy. Suggest adding a canary route that pins to cerberus-int8.gguf and fallback policy to cerberus-fp16 when quality regressions exceed threshold. We'll need a rollout plan: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with monitoring hooks.

eva: I built the targeted Spanish suite: 200 prompts, labelled answers + golden refs. I'll upload to s3://redwood-evals/cerberus/spanish_suite_v1.json by EOD.

sam: After sensitivity sweep, plan for two candidate builds: cerberus-int8.gguf and cerberus-hybrid-fp8.gguf. For each build run:
- token-level perf (tokens/s) on p4d and a100
- regression A/B vs fp16 on multilingual + hallucination suite
- automatic quality checks: perplexity, QA-F1, token divergence

nina: Owner matrix:
- smoke + baseline numbers: sam (today)
- per-layer sensitivity + hybrid plan: dmitri (tomorrow)
- spanish suite and targeted evals: eva (EOD)
- gguf conversion + canary rollout: oncall-ops (next Tues)
- final cost/perf report: nina (post-run)

dmitri: I'll run the sensitivity sweep now and post results here. Expect JSON + heatmap PNG. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

eval-bot: NOTE: please tag runs with `cerberus-2401007890` for tracking.

nina: Awesome. One more ask: include prompt-conditioning tests (few-shot vs zero-shot) to check for increased hallucination under quant. Add to the harness.

sam: I'll add the conditioning dimension to the eval harness. Minimal timeline: smoke today, sens sweep tomorrow, candidate builds within 48-72h, canary next week.

nina: Great. Action items pinned. Thanks team. :rocket:
